source.title: Seeing the Threat: Vulnerabilities in Vision-Language Models to Adversarial Attack
source.authors: Juan Ren; M. Dras; Usman Naseem

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. It contains some typographical/OCR errors, but no apparent cutoff affecting the reported results.
record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates multimodal adversarial attacks on vision-language models. It does not test fine-tuning safety erosion, response-position KL, compliant-token prefilling, suffix or decoding bypasses, safety localization in parameters, or training to deepen safety.
record.gate_note: The paper reports harmful-prompt response outcomes under image-based and cross-modal attacks. These are related findings about LVLM vulnerabilities, but do not test any listed claim version: the attacks are not the fine-tuning interventions or token-opening mechanisms specified in those versions. Rows record the table's non-refusal rates, non-following rates, and ASR grades under those attacks. The paper's representation analysis is qualitative and does not measure any listed version.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates multimodal jailbreak datasets (AdvBench image perturbations, FigStep, MM-SafetyBench, SIUO) on four LVLMs. It runs no fine-tuning, no per-token KL, no prefilling, suffix or decoding attack, and no parameter localization or deepening training. It cites Qi et al. 2023b only as background on safety loss from fine-tuning. Its results do not bear on any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Partly right. The authors conclude that models without OCR (LLaVA, Llama 3.2) still encode semantic cues from typographic images that enable harmful instruction following. OCR-equipped models (Qwen 2.5, InternVL) remain susceptible, which the authors attribute to weak cross-modal alignment. They propose a two-stage evaluation that separates refusal, instruction non-following and attack success, and scores harm on a Likert scale. They call for both robust visual understanding and fine-grained alignment.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates multimodal adversarial attack datasets; it does not reproduce the fine-tuning or token-position methods in the cited original sources.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported outcomes vary by model and dataset; the authors state that removing professional-advice examples from scoring reduces ASR and ASR Quality scores.

fits_no_version.finding: LVLM non-refusal on harmful multimodal prompts ranges from 2% (AdvBench) to 83% (SIUO, InternVL) and depends strongly on attack type and model (Table 1).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Cross-modal and implicit-intent attacks elicit harmful compliance from LVLMs far more than image-perturbation attacks.

fits_no_version.finding: Llama 3.2 Vision fails to follow instructions in 33–89% of cases, which makes its low non-refusal rates partly a capability or over-refusal artefact.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Instruction non-following confounds attack-success rates in LVLM safety evaluations.

fits_no_version.finding: Normalized ASR quality scores range from 0.49 to 0.90 across models and datasets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: How harmful LVLM compliant responses are varies by model and attack dataset.

record.problems: The study is limited to four datasets and four model families. It reports no uncertainty estimates or control comparisons. Evaluation relies on model-based judgments with human checking of edge cases, not large-scale human annotation. The text names GPT-4o-mini for evaluation in the methodology but GPT-4.1-mini in the limitations. The authors note that some SIUO examples and professional-advice cases involve subjective judgments.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted the table's hard-refusal, soft-refusal, and partial-refusal category percentages because the 48 retained rows prioritize non-refusal, non-following, and ASR grade outcomes most relevant to harmful-response behaviour. These categories appear in Table 1.

untested.parts: No harmful-data fine-tuning; Qi et al. 2023b is cited only as background.
No aligned-versus-base per-token KL or analysis by response position.
No prefilled compliant opening, text suffix or decoding change. The image-based attacks are a different mechanism from the opening-token bypass.
No weight or rank localization. The visual-token projection analysis is not about safety parameters.
No test of data or objective as the cause of shallowness.
No deepening or safety training is evaluated.

record.verdict_notes: The record's relation 'discusses' is changed to 'cites_only': the original source appears only in a background sentence about catastrophic forgetting. The rows are correctly unlinked to any version. Table 1's Total row gives an InternVL ASR grade of 1.43, which exceeds the stated [0,1] normalization. The paper names GPT-4o-mini as the judge in its methodology but GPT-4.1-mini in its limitations. The omission of the hard, soft and partial refusal categories is declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: No harmful-example fine-tuning or post-fine-tuning refusal/compliance comparison.
No aligned-versus-base per-token KL measurement or response-position analysis.
No compliant-opening prefilling, adversarial suffix, or decoding-change test; the study evaluates multimodal image and cross-modal attacks instead.
No analysis or edit of weights or ranks to localize safety behaviour.
No test of whether training data or objectives cause safety shallowness.
No training intended to deepen safety or evaluation of whether such training holds up.
